nodes.label: atomicity
nodes.def: The all-or-nothing property: a transaction's effects are either fully applied or fully absent; implemented via undo_log and transaction rollback.

nodes.label: c009
nodes.def: commit completion: the terminal state transition from active to committed; releases all locks held exclusively and schedules release of shared locks per protocol

nodes.label: isolation level
nodes.def: A configurable parameter defining the degree to which concurrent transactions are isolated from each other's uncommitted or intermediate effects.

nodes.label: aborted state
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after rollback completes; all acquired locks are released and the transaction cannot be restarted automatically.

nodes.label: committed data
nodes.def: database state resulting from successfully completed transactions; constitutes the visible universe for read_committed queries

nodes.label: rollback
nodes.def: The act of undoing a transaction's effects using undo_log entries, returning the database to its pre-transaction state.

nodes.label: tl log record
nodes.def: The fundamental unit of a transaction_log: a single append-only entry recording one atomic change or lifecycle event made by a transaction; identified by an lsn.

nodes.label: transaction state
nodes.def: The current phase of a transaction lifecycle: active, partially_committed, committed, aborted; drives lock release and recovery behavior.

nodes.label: read committed
nodes.def: An isolation_level where each statement sees only data committed before that statement begins; prevents dirty_read but allows non_repeatable_read and phantom_read.

nodes.label: rr definition
nodes.def: An isolation_level ensuring that all reads within a transaction see a consistent snapshot of the database as of transaction start; prevents non_repeatable_read by acquiring and hol

nodes.label: commit
nodes.def: The act of making a transaction's effects permanent: flush log records to durable storage, release locks, transition transaction_state to committed.

nodes.label: row level locking
nodes.def: Lock management at the individual row granularity via row_lock entries in lock_manager's lock table; enables high concurrency but increases lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: acid properties
nodes.def: The four guarantees of database transactions: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability — the foundational contract between a DBMS and its clients.

nodes.label: concurrency control
nodes.def: The set of mechanisms a DBMS uses to manage simultaneous access to shared data while preserving correctness and isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: database transaction
nodes.def: A logical unit of work executed against a database, bounded by BEGIN and COMMIT/ROLLBACK, guaranteeing ACID properties across one or more SQL operations.

nodes.label: dirty read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction reads data written by another transaction that has not yet committed; only possible in read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: dur recovery manager
nodes.def: The subsystem that enforces durability by reconstructing the committed database state from transaction_log after a crash; scans log forward to redo committed changes and backward t

nodes.label: dur write ahead logging
nodes.def: A protocol mandating that log records describing modifications be flushed to durable_storage before the corresponding data pages are written to disk; foundational mechanism for bot

nodes.label: rr read lock
nodes.def: A shared_lock acquired when a row is read under repeatable_read; held until transaction commits or rolls back, preventing any concurrent transaction from acquiring a write_lock on

nodes.label: tl recovery manager
nodes.def: The subsystem that, on system restart, reads the transaction_log from the last tl_checkpoint_record forward; replays committed tl_redo_log entries and rolls back uncommitted transa

nodes.label: transaction log
nodes.def: An append-only sequence of records tracking every change made by transactions; the primary mechanism for atomicity and durability.

nodes.label: write ahead logging
nodes.def: A protocol requiring log records be flushed to durable storage before the corresponding data changes are applied; ensures durability and atomicity.

nodes.label: c001
nodes.def: commit point: the precise instant when a transaction transitions from active to committed; the log sequence number position where durable persistence is guaranteed

nodes.label: commit visibility boundary
nodes.def: temporal threshold in read_committed: a datum is visible iff its committing_transaction committed before the reading statement started

nodes.label: deadlock detection
nodes.def: The process of identifying when a deadlock has formed, typically via a wait_for_graph analyzed by lock_manager.

nodes.label: exclusive lock
nodes.def: A lock type granting sole read-write access to a resource; incompatible with all other lock types including shared_lock and update_lock.

nodes.label: rr lock based
nodes.def: repeatable_read uses a locking_protocol based on shared_locks on rows and optionally index_range_locks on key ranges rather than snapshot versioning.

nodes.label: rr lock duration
nodes.def: The temporal scope from row_read acquisition of read_lock until transaction_boundary where atomicity resolves via commit or rollback, releasing all held locks.

nodes.label: undo log
nodes.def: Log records describing the previous state of modified data; used to undo uncommitted transaction changes during rollback and recovery.

nodes.label: write lock held until commit
nodes.def: exclusive lock discipline in read_committed requiring a transaction to hold write locks on modified rows until transaction commit or rollback

nodes.label: abort reason
nodes.def: The specific cause that precipitated a transaction's transition to the aborted_state, such as a constraint violation, deadlock detection timeout, explicit ROLLBACK request, or appl

nodes.label: aborted data
nodes.def: The intermediate state of rows modified by a transaction that later aborted; the partial_effects_undone that existed between the first write and the rollback completion, representa

nodes.label: before image
nodes.def: The committed database state of a row immediately before a transaction modifies it; recorded in the undo_log so the modification can be undone if the transaction rolls back.

nodes.label: committed
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after durable persistence of all changes; locks are released per locking_protocol rules.

nodes.label: compensation action
nodes.def: A corrective operation executed when forward undo via undo_log is impossible; used in distributed systems where original transaction steps cannot be directly reversed, preserving a

nodes.label: dur log flush
nodes.def: The synchronous I/O operation that transfers log buffers from volatile memory to durable_storage; must complete before commit returns success to the client.

nodes.label: dur redo log
nodes.def: Log records describing the after-image of modified data; during recovery the manager reapplies these records to restore committed transaction effects.

nodes.label: dur undo log
nodes.def: Log records describing the before-image of modified data; used during rollback and recovery to reverse uncommitted changes, preserving durability by ensuring only committed effects

nodes.label: lock granularity
nodes.def: The size of the database object protected by a lock: row_lock, page_lock, table_lock — trading off concurrency against lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: read uncommitted
nodes.def: The weakest isolation_level: transactions may observe uncommitted changes from other transactions, permitting dirty_read.

nodes.label: recovery log entry
nodes.def: A durable record written to the transaction log capturing a single row modification, containing the transaction identifier, the affected row identifier, the before_image, and the a

nodes.label: statement
nodes.def: A single SQL operation within a transaction; atomicity requires that each statement either fully completes its effect or fully reverts before the next statement begins.

nodes.label: statement level read consistency
nodes.def: guarantee within read_committed that each SQL statement sees all changes committed at the moment that statement began execution

nodes.label: tl checkpoint record
nodes.def: A special log_record written periodically by a checkpoint_writer; records the volatile database state at a consistent point, bounding the recovery_manager's replay horizon.

nodes.label: tl flush to disk
nodes.def: The act of transferring the contents of tl_log_buffer to durable storage; triggered by transaction commit, tl_log_buffer overflow, or a periodic checkpoint; O(1) or O(n) bounded by

nodes.label: tl undo log
nodes.def: A structured collection of tl_update_record entries chained by a transaction; traversed in reverse order during rollback to restore the before_image of each modified entity.

nodes.label: tl update record
nodes.def: A log_record capturing a before_image and after_image of a modified data page or row; used by both redo_recovery (for durability) and undo_recovery (for atomicity rollback).

nodes.label: transaction boundary
nodes.def: The demarcation point between consecutive transaction executions defining the scope over which atomicity applies; all effects within are committed or none are, with no partial visi

nodes.label: transaction id
nodes.def: A monotonically increasing identifier assigned to each transaction; the basis for snapshot_isolation read_view construction and visibility_check.

nodes.label: two phase locking
nodes.def: A locking_protocol where transactions must acquire all locks during a growing_phase and release all locks during a shrinking_phase, guaranteeing conflict_serializable schedules.

nodes.label: uncommitted change
nodes.def: A modification to database state made by a transaction that has not yet committed; visible to other transactions at read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: all or nothing
nodes.def: The conceptual guarantee that a transaction executes as an indivisible unit: either every operation succeeds or no operation has any effect.

nodes.label: automatic restart forbidden
nodes.def: A protocol constraint requiring that a transaction in the aborted_state cannot be re-executed automatically by the database; the application must explicitly reissue the transaction

nodes.label: c002
nodes.def: commit log record: the write-ahead log entry that atomically records the commit point; contains transaction identifier and commit LSN

nodes.label: c003
nodes.def: commit sequence number (CSN): a monotonically incrementing identifier assigned to each committed transaction; provides total ordering of committed state changes

nodes.label: c004
nodes.def: commit durability: the guaranteed persistence property that all writes of a committed transaction survive system crashes; realized via write-ahead log

nodes.label: c005
nodes.def: commit visibility: the isolation property that all writes of a committed transaction become visible to subsequent read_committed queries in other transactions

nodes.label: c006
nodes.def: commit LSN: the log sequence number position of the commit log record; the fence above which all prior transaction writes are durable

nodes.label: c014
nodes.def: commit decision: the coordinator's recorded choice (commit or abort) in two-phase commit; propagates to all participants

nodes.label: connection pool limiting
nodes.def: A concurrency control mechanism restricting the number of concurrent database connections to bound resource usage and lock_contention.

nodes.label: consistency
nodes.def: A transaction transforms the database from one valid state to another, preserving all defined integrity constraints and business rules.

nodes.label: database pool exhaustion
nodes.def: A failure condition where all connections in a connection_pool are consumed by blocked transactions waiting for locks, preventing new transactions from starting.

nodes.label: deadlock prevention
nodes.def: Protocols that ensure deadlocks cannot occur by ordering lock acquisition or assigning priorities that determine which transaction rolls back.

nodes.label: dur checkpoint
nodes.def: A periodic snapshot of the database state written to durable_storage that bounds recovery time by reducing the log interval that must be scanned during crash_recovery.

nodes.label: dur commit persistence
nodes.def: The committed transaction_state transition where all redo_log entries are guaranteed durable and the transaction is guaranteed to survive any subsequent crash.

nodes.label: dur crash recovery
nodes.def: The process of restarting the database and using transaction_log to reconstruct the committed_data state as of the moment of crash, ensuring no durability contract is broken.

nodes.label: dur durable storage
nodes.def: The physical medium or storage subsystem that guarantees bitwise persistence of written data across power loss, hardware failure, and system crashes; the endpoint of all durability

nodes.label: isolation
nodes.def: The property that concurrently executing transactions do not interfere with each other; the degree of interference is controlled by isolation_level.

nodes.label: lock contention
nodes.def: A performance condition where many transactions compete for the same locks, causing lock_wait and degrading throughput; mitigated by lock_granularity tuning.

nodes.label: lock release
nodes.def: The deterministic act of relinquishing every lock held by a transaction upon reaching its transaction_boundary, whether through commit or abort, restoring exclusive or shared acces

nodes.label: lock timeout handling
nodes.def: timeout mechanism in read_committed for transactions blocked waiting to acquire conflicting locks on rows

nodes.label: locking protocol
nodes.def: A disciplined set of rules governing when locks may be acquired and released to ensure serializability or other isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: no dirty reads
nodes.def: the guaranteed anomaly prevention in read_committed: a transaction may never observe uncommitted changes from concurrent transactions

nodes.label: non repeatable read possible
nodes.def: the permitted anomaly in read_committed: a transaction reading the same row twice may observe different values if a concurrent transaction updates and commits that row between read

nodes.label: optimistic cc
nodes.def: Concurrency control strategy that permits unrestricted execution and detects conflicts only at validation_phase, aborting and retrying on conflict.

nodes.label: partial effects undone
nodes.def: The invariant that upon rollback all modifications performed by the transaction are reversed to match the before_image recorded in each recovery_log_entry, leaving no residual trac

nodes.label: partial state prevention
nodes.def: The enforcement mechanism ensuring that if a transaction fails at any point before transaction_boundary, no tuple modifications leak into committed_data; achieved by deferring all

nodes.label: phantom read possible
nodes.def: the permitted anomaly in read_committed: a transaction executing the same range query twice may observe different row sets if concurrent transactions insert or delete rows within t

nodes.label: read lock release
nodes.def: lock management characteristic in read_committed where shared read locks are typically released immediately after each row access rather than held to transaction end

nodes.label: recovery manager
nodes.def: The component responsible for restoring database consistency after failure using transaction_log and ARIES_recovery.

nodes.label: rr first commit wins
nodes.def: When two transactions under snapshot_isolation both attempt to modify the same row the first to commit wins and the second rolls back; not applicable to lock-based repeatable_read.

nodes.label: rr gap lock
nodes.def: An index_range_lock on the gap between index entries acquired under repeatable_read to prevent phantom_read by blocking insert operations in that range.

nodes.label: rr lock timeout
nodes.def: A mechanism to prevent indefinite blocking when write_lock acquisition is stalled by read_locks held under repeatable_read; transaction rolls back if lock not acquired within thres

nodes.label: rr observation window
nodes.def: The interval from transaction_start to the rr_transaction_boundary during which a repeatable_read transaction observes a frozen snapshot of the database; any rows committed by othe

nodes.label: rr phantom read
nodes.def: A read phenomenon in weaker isolation levels where a transaction re-executing a ranged query sees new rows inserted by a concurrent transaction between executions; under rr_isolati

nodes.label: rr phantom read residual
nodes.def: repeatable_read permits phantom_read when gap_lock is not enforced on the index used by the query; inserts in gaps between locked rows remain possible.

nodes.label: rr rollback
nodes.def: The rollback operation executed by a transaction under repeatable_read, undoing all row modifications using recovery_log_entry before_image data, releasing all held rr_read_locks v

nodes.label: rr transaction snapshot
nodes.def: The committed_data visible to a repeatable_read transaction is frozen at transaction_start regardless of later commits by concurrent transactions.

nodes.label: rr transaction state
nodes.def: The phase of a transaction executing under repeatable_read, following the standard transaction_state lifecycle of active, partially_committed, committed, or aborted, where each pha

nodes.label: rr write lock prevention
nodes.def: A write_lock request on a row already held with a read_lock by another transaction blocks until that transaction releases its locks at commit or rollback.

nodes.label: serializable
nodes.def: The strongest isolation_level: the result of executing concurrent transactions is equivalent to some serial order of those transactions; prevents all anomalies.

nodes.label: snapshot isolation
nodes.def: An isolation_level using mvcc where a transaction reads from a consistent snapshot taken at transaction start; prevents lost_update but allows write_skew.

nodes.label: statement start timestamp
nodes.def: logical moment recorded when each statement begins, establishing the visibility cutoff point for read_committed row versions

nodes.label: strict two phase locking
nodes.def: A variant of two_phase_locking where exclusive_locks are held until transaction end, ensuring strict_schedule and enabling cascading_less schedules.

nodes.label: timestamp ordering
nodes.def: A concurrency control method assigning timestamps to transactions and using them to order operations, ensuring serializability without locking.

nodes.label: tl abort record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction enters the aborted_state; signals that undo_log entries must be applied to reverse this transaction's effects.

nodes.label: tl checkpoint writer
nodes.def: The subsystem component that periodically writes a tl_checkpoint_record to the transaction_log; trims obsolete log segments and bounds crash_recovery time.

nodes.label: tl commit record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction commits; marks the durable persistence boundary for durability guarantees; flushed to disk before the transaction releases its locks.

nodes.label: tl dirty page table
nodes.def: A runtime data structure maintained by recovery_manager listing data pages modified but not yet flushed; consulted during checkpoint to ensure write_ahead_logging invariants hold.

nodes.label: tl redo log
nodes.def: A log_record or series of tl_update_record entries capturing the after_image of modifications; replayed by recovery_manager to idempotently reconstruct committed changes after a cr

nodes.label: tl wal protocol
nodes.def: Write-Ahead Logging: the protocol requiring that a tl_log_record be flushed to durable storage before the corresponding data modification is written to the database page; the prima

nodes.label: transaction read
nodes.def: The act of a transaction executing a read operation; at read_uncommitted this read may return uncommitted_change from concurrent transactions.

nodes.label: update lock
nodes.def: A lock type that prevents deadlock during lock_upgrade: compatible with shared_lock but not with other update_locks or exclusive_locks.

nodes.label: write lock not required
nodes.def: The characteristic of read_uncommitted where a writing transaction does not hold an exclusive lock preventing other transactions from reading its uncommitted state.

nodes.label: aborted state contains abort reason
nodes.def: aborted_state captures the abort_reason that triggered rollback: constraint_violation, deadlock_timeout, user_abort, or system_failure.

nodes.label: aborted state contains partial effects undone
nodes.def: aborted_state records the partial_effects_undone: the set of modifications that were rolled back to their before-images.

nodes.label: aborted state creates recovery log entry
nodes.def: aborted_state causes the recovery_log to persist an abort record enabling redo-undo recovery procedures.

nodes.label: aborted state forbids automatic restart
nodes.def: aborted_state encodes the automatic_restart_forbidden property; a new transaction must be initiated explicitly.

nodes.label: aborted state is terminal transaction state
nodes.def: aborted_state is the terminal transaction_state reached when rollback completes; no state transitions emanate from it.

nodes.label: aborted state records transaction id
nodes.def: aborted_state records the transaction_id of the transaction that entered the terminal state for recovery audit.

nodes.label: aborted state signals lock release
nodes.def: aborted_state signals the release of all locks acquired by the transaction under the locking_protocol; no locks persist into aborted_state.

nodes.label: aborted state yields aborted data visibility
nodes.def: aborted_state produces aborted_data that is invisible to committed_data consumers under the isolation_level; other transactions perceive no effect.

nodes.label: active state
nodes.def: The initial transaction_state: transaction is executing, holding locks, accumulating changes in transaction_log.

nodes.label: advisory lock
nodes.def: An application-defined lock with no automatic database effect; the application is responsible for enforcing its meaning and usage pattern.

nodes.label: after image
nodes.def: The state of a row resulting from a transaction's modification; stored for redo in write_ahead_logging systems to guarantee durability alongside atomicity.

nodes.label: aries recovery
nodes.def: The Algorithm for Recovery and Isolation Exploiting Semantics: a precise recovery procedure using transaction_log, undo_log, and redo_log to achieve atomicity and durability.

nodes.label: auto commit
nodes.def: A mode where each individual SQL statement is implicitly wrapped in its own transaction, committing immediately upon statement completion.

nodes.label: basic timestamp protocol
nodes.def: A timestamp_ordering scheme where each data item maintains read_timestamp and write_timestamp; transactions violating these abort.

nodes.label: c007
nodes.def: commit barrier: the synchronization point ensuring all prior transaction writes are flushed to durable storage before any subsequent transaction commits

nodes.label: c008
nodes.def: commit acknowledgment: the confirmation signal returned to the client indicating successful durable persistence of the transaction

nodes.label: c010
nodes.def: commit promise: the contractual guarantee to the user that transaction effects are durable and will survive any subsequent system restart

nodes.label: c011
nodes.def: commit propagation: the process by which committed transaction effects become visible in the committed_data universe accessible to read_committed queries

nodes.label: c012
nodes.def: group commit: an optimization that batches multiple transaction commit operations into a single durable write to improve throughput

nodes.label: c013
nodes.def: commit vote: in distributed commit protocols the yes vote from a participant indicating readiness to commit; required before coordinator records decision

nodes.label: c015
nodes.def: commit timestamp: the wall-clock time recorded when commit point is established; used for versioning and serialization in timestamp-based CC

nodes.label: cap theorem
nodes.def: A theorem stating that a distributed system can provide at most two of three properties: consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

nodes.label: cascadeless schedule
nodes.def: A recoverable_schedule where transactions only read data committed before the transaction began; prevents cascading aborts.

nodes.label: causal consistency
nodes.def: A consistency model guaranteeing that causally related operations appear in order across all nodes; weaker than strong_consistency but stronger than eventual_consistency_level.

nodes.label: checkpoint
nodes.def: A consistent point-in-time snapshot of the database state written to durable storage, reducing recovery time by bounding how far recovery must replay logs.

nodes.label: clip xmin
nodes.def: The oldest active transaction_id below which all row versions are guaranteed visible to all current transactions.

nodes.label: committed before statement
nodes.def: A temporal boundary condition: only modifications committed before the statement_start are visible; uncommitted changes are invisible.

nodes.label: committed version
nodes.def: The state of a row or data item after its modifying transaction has committed, making it visible to concurrent read_committed statements.

nodes.label: compare and swap
nodes.def: An atomic primitive that atomically compares a memory value with an expected value and swaps it if equal; used in lock_free_cc for conflict-free updates.

nodes.label: compare and swap pattern
nodes.def: An optimistic_cc pattern using compare_and_swap on a version or sequence number to detect concurrent modifications without locking.

nodes.label: compensating transaction
nodes.def: A reverse operation executed to undo the effects of a saga step when a subsequent step fails, restoring the system to a consistent state.

nodes.label: compensation
nodes.def: The compensatory action taken to reverse a transaction's effects, encompassing rollback via undo_log as the primary compensation mechanism.

nodes.label: concurrency level
nodes.def: A configuration parameter (often database pool size) controlling the maximum number of concurrent transactions or connections.

nodes.label: conflict detection
nodes.def: The mechanism in optimistic_cc determining whether a transaction's read_set or write_set overlaps with another transaction's write_set in a forbidden way.

nodes.label: conflict serializable
nodes.def: A schedule property where serializability can be proven by analyzing the conflict graph of read/write operations; achievable with strict_two_phase_locking.

nodes.label: consensus protocol
nodes.def: A distributed algorithm enabling distributed_transaction participants to agree on a single value or decision; used alongside two_phase_commit for fault tolerance.

nodes.label: conservative two phase locking
nodes.def: A variant of two_phase_locking where all locks are acquired before the transaction begins, eliminating deadlock entirely at the cost of reduced concurrency.

nodes.label: cursor stability
nodes.def: An isolation_level specific to cursor-based reads: locks are held only on the current row, providing a middle ground between read_uncommitted and read_committed.

nodes.label: deadlock
nodes.def: A cycle of transactions each waiting to acquire a lock held by the next transaction in the cycle, causing all involved transactions to block indefinitely.

nodes.label: deadlock detection interval
nodes.def: The frequency with which lock_manager runs deadlock detection; shorter intervals catch deadlocks faster at higher CPU cost.

nodes.label: deadlock frequency
nodes.def: The rate at which deadlocks occur in the system; indicates whether deadlock_prevention or deadlock_detection thresholds need tuning.

nodes.label: dirty write
nodes.def: An anomaly where one transaction overwrites an uncommitted value written by another transaction, violating atomicity and potentially causing inconsistency.

nodes.label: distributed locking
nodes.def: Lock management across multiple database nodes using a distributed lock service; required for distributed_transaction coordination.

nodes.label: distributed transaction
nodes.def: A transaction spanning multiple database nodes or storage systems; requires coordination protocols like two_phase_commit for atomicity.

nodes.label: durability
nodes.def: Once a transaction commits, its effects persist permanently even after system crash; guaranteed by write_ahead_logging and recovery_manager.

nodes.label: eventual consistency
nodes.def: A consistency model where updates propagate asynchronously and all replicas converge to the same state given no new updates; relevant in distributed_transaction.

nodes.label: lock based read committed
nodes.def: A read_committed implementation variant using shared locks acquired at read time but released before transaction commit, permitting non-repeatable reads.

nodes.label: lock manager
nodes.def: The subsystem responsible for tracking held locks, responding to lock requests, building the wait_for_graph, and detecting deadlocks.

nodes.label: lock upgrade
nodes.def: The conversion of a held shared_lock to an exclusive_lock; requires checking lock_compatibility_matrix and may block or fail if incompatible locks exist.

nodes.label: mvcc
nodes.def: Multi-version concurrency control: maintain multiple versions of rows so readers and writers do not block each other, each transaction sees a snapshot.

nodes.label: non repeatable read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction reads the same row twice and gets different values because another transaction modified and committed between reads.

nodes.label: observation window
nodes.def: The temporal scope during which a reading transaction may see uncommitted changes from other transactions, bounded by those transactions' commit operations.

nodes.label: page lock
nodes.def: A lock_granularity unit protecting a disk page (typically 4–16 KB); intermediate granularity used in some storage engines.

nodes.label: paxos consensus
nodes.def: A consensus_protocol for reaching agreement in a distributed system with faulty nodes; provides safety guarantees even under network_partition.

nodes.label: pessimistic cc
nodes.def: Concurrency control strategy that prevents conflicts by acquiring locks before accessing data, blocking if locks are unavailable.

nodes.label: phantom read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction re-executes a range query and gets a different set of rows due to another transaction inserting or deleting rows in that range.

nodes.label: recovery subsystem
nodes.def: The database component responsible for restoring consistency after a crash by scanning the transaction log, classifying each transaction as committed uncommitted or aborted, and ex

nodes.label: repeatable read
nodes.def: An isolation_level ensuring that all reads within a transaction see a consistent snapshot as of transaction start; prevents non_repeatable_read but may permit phantom_read.

nodes.label: row lock
nodes.def: A lock_granularity unit protecting a single row; maximum concurrency but highest lock_manager overhead and risk of lock_contention.

nodes.label: rr blocking vs optimistic
nodes.def: repeatable_read employs pessimistic locking that blocks concurrent writers at read time, unlike optimistic concurrency control which detects conflicts at commit time.

nodes.label: rr commit
nodes.def: The commit event in a transaction executing under repeatable_read, marking the transaction_boundary at which all held rr_read_locks undergo lock_release and the transaction's effec

nodes.label: rr committed data
nodes.def: Database rows that have been durably persisted by a committed transaction and fall within the rr_observation_window of a concurrent repeatable_read transaction; these rows are visi

nodes.label: rr isolation level
nodes.def: The isolation_level at which a transaction sees only data committed before its start, acquires a shared rr_read_lock on every row it reads, holds all such locks until transaction_b

nodes.label: rr non repeatable read prevention
nodes.def: The guarantee that repeating the same row read within a transaction always returns the same before_image; achieved by holding read_lock preventing concurrent write_lock acquisition

nodes.label: rr transaction boundary
nodes.def: The moment when a repeatable_read transaction terminates via commit or rollback, concluding the rr_observation_window and triggering lock_release of all rr_read_locks acquired duri

nodes.label: rr versus read committed
nodes.def: read_committed releases read_locks after each statement, permitting non_repeatable_read; repeatable_read holds read_locks through transaction_end, eliminating that anomaly.

nodes.label: rr versus snapshot isolation
nodes.def: repeatable_read uses write_lock blocking while snapshot_isolation uses mvcc versioning; snapshot_isolation prevents non_repeatable_read but allows write_skew that repeatable_read p

nodes.label: rr write ahead logging
nodes.def: The write_ahead_logging requirement within a lock-based repeatable_read system mandating that every recovery_log_entry be flushed to durable storage before the corresponding row mo

nodes.label: shared lock
nodes.def: A lock type permitting concurrent reads by multiple transactions but preventing exclusive writes; compatible with other shared_locks, incompatible with exclusive_lock.

nodes.label: strict schedule
nodes.def: A schedule where reads and writes of a data item occur in the same order as in a serial schedule; required for strict_two_phase_locking and ARIES recovery.

nodes.label: strong strict two phase locking
nodes.def: strict_two_phase_locking where all locks (shared and exclusive) are held until transaction end, the most common production locking_protocol.

nodes.label: table lock
nodes.def: A lock_granularity unit protecting an entire table; high lock_manager efficiency but low concurrency for partitioned or sparse tables.

nodes.label: tl begin record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction transitions to the active transaction_state; records transaction_id and start timestamp but no data modifications.

nodes.label: tl log buffer
nodes.def: A volatile in-memory page or ring buffer where tl_log_record entries are assembled before flush; resides in the transaction's write_ahead_logging envelope and is flushed as a whole

nodes.label: tl lsn
nodes.def: Log Sequence Number: a monotonically increasing numeric identifier assigned to each tl_log_record; enables total ordering, O(1) record retrieval, and dependency tracking between lo

nodes.label: transaction snapshot
nodes.def: The consistent view of the database state constructed at a transaction's start point, containing all rows whose committing transactions committed before that moment and excluding u

nodes.label: two phase commit 2pc
nodes.def: The two-phase commit protocol coordinating commit of a distributed_transaction across participant nodes: coordinator asks prepare then commit/abort.

nodes.label: uncommitted version
nodes.def: The state of a row or data item modified by an active uncommitted transaction, invisible to read_committed statements.

nodes.label: write write conflict
nodes.def: A conflict between two transactions attempting to modify the same data item; prevented by exclusive_lock or last_writer-wins in mvcc.

nodes.label: eventual consistency level
nodes.def: A consistency model where reads may return stale data but the system guarantees convergence after all writes propagate and settle.

nodes.label: exponential backoff
nodes.def: A retry strategy where the delay before each transaction_retry doubles exponentially, reducing contention and thundering herd on shared resources.

nodes.label: for update nowait
nodes.def: A select_for_update variant that fails immediately if any requested lock cannot be acquired rather than blocking.

nodes.label: for update skip locked
nodes.def: A select_for_update variant that skips rows already locked by other transactions, returning only rows that can be locked immediately.

nodes.label: frozen xid
nodes.def: A special transaction_id older than all normal transaction_ids; row versions with frozen_xid are always visible and never garbage collected.

nodes.label: gap lock
nodes.def: A lock on an index interval between two consecutive index entries; used by next_key_locking to prevent phantom_read in range queries.

nodes.label: garbage collection mvcc
nodes.def: The process of reclaiming row versions no longer needed by any active transaction's read_view to reclaim storage.

nodes.label: idempotency
nodes.def: The property that executing an operation multiple times has the same effect as executing it once; essential for safe transaction_retry in unreliable networks.

nodes.label: index locking
nodes.def: Lock management for B-tree or hash index pages to protect structural changes during concurrent index operations.

nodes.label: index only scan mvcc
nodes.def: An index scan in mvcc that satisfies a query without accessing the heap by checking visibility against index-only tuples.

nodes.label: innodb locking
nodes.def: MySQL InnoDB's concurrency control combining gap_lock, next_key_locking, and a sophisticated lock_manager supporting all isolation levels.

nodes.label: intention lock
nodes.def: A lock mode indicating intent to acquire finer-grained locks on sub-objects; used at higher levels of lock_granularity hierarchy (table, page, row).

nodes.label: isolation level configuration
nodes.def: The database-specific syntax and knobs for setting isolation_level (SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL in SQL, engine-specific params).

nodes.label: isolation level performance
nodes.def: The inverse relationship between isolation_level strength and throughput: stronger isolation requires more locking or version management overhead.

nodes.label: isolation level tradeoffs
nodes.def: The explicit performance vs correctness choices made when selecting an isolation_level; stronger guarantees reduce concurrency and throughput.

nodes.label: key lock
nodes.def: An index-based lock protecting a specific index entry; used in next_key_locking to prevent phantom_read by locking index gaps.

nodes.label: linearizability
nodes.def: A strong consistency model for distributed systems where operations appear atomic and instantaneous to all observers; stronger than serializable in some respects.

nodes.label: livelock
nodes.def: A condition where transactions repeatedly restart or change state in response to other transactions without making progress, distinct from deadlock.

nodes.label: lock acquisition
nodes.def: The act of requesting and obtaining a lock from lock_manager before performing a read or write operation on a protected resource.

nodes.label: lock chain analysis
nodes.def: A diagnostic technique tracing which transactions hold and wait on locks to identify sources of lock_contention.

nodes.label: lock compatibility matrix
nodes.def: A table specifying which lock modes can be held simultaneously on the same object; drives lock acquisition decisions in lock_manager.

nodes.label: lock escalation
nodes.def: A mechanism where lock_manager automatically upgrades many fine-grained locks to a coarser lock when lock_contention thresholds are exceeded.

nodes.label: lock free cc
nodes.def: Concurrency control techniques that avoid blocking through atomic operations rather than locks; compare_and_swap is the canonical primitive.

nodes.label: lock manager impl
nodes.def: The concrete implementation of lock_manager managing lock tables, queues, compatibility checks, and deadlock detection.

nodes.label: lock timeout
nodes.def: A mechanism where a transaction waiting for a lock is aborted after a configurable elapsed period, preventing indefinite waiting.

nodes.label: lock wait
nodes.def: A state where a transaction cannot proceed because the resource it needs is locked by another transaction; resolved by lock_manager upon lock release.

nodes.label: lock wait time
nodes.def: The cumulative time transactions spend blocked waiting for locks; a key metric for diagnosing lock_contention and lock_manager bottlenecks.

nodes.label: lock wait timeout
nodes.def: A mechanism where a lock_wait is abandoned after a configured duration, returning an error to the application for retry or handling.

nodes.label: log sequence number
nodes.def: A monotonically increasing identifier for log records in write_ahead_logging; used to order recovery operations and coordinate replication.

nodes.label: lost update
nodes.def: An anomaly where two transactions both read and update the same row, and one update overwrites the other's change because of write_write_conflict.

nodes.label: mongodb concurrency
nodes.def: MongoDB's lock_manager using intent locks at database and collection levels, with optimistic writes and retry on lock acquisition failure.

nodes.label: multi version timestamp protocol
nodes.def: A timestamp_ordering scheme using mvcc: readers never block writers, writers never block readers, and conflicts trigger abort.

nodes.label: mvcc read committed
nodes.def: A read_committed implementation variant using multi-version concurrency control where statements read the most recent committed version of each row.

nodes.label: nested transaction
nodes.def: A transaction contained within another transaction, with its own commit/rollback semantics that may be independent or subordinated to the parent.

nodes.label: network partition
nodes.def: A failure mode where nodes in a distributed system cannot communicate with each other; forces a choice between availability and consistency per CAP_theorem.

nodes.label: next key locking
nodes.def: A locking_protocol combining row_lock on the accessed record with gap_lock on the surrounding interval to prevent phantom_read.

nodes.label: optimistic locking version column
nodes.def: A pattern where a version integer is incremented on each row update and checked during transaction commit to detect concurrent modifications.

nodes.label: oracle read consistency
nodes.def: Oracle Database's implementation of statement-level read consistency using undo segments to reconstruct read_view at query start.

nodes.label: pacelc model
nodes.def: An extension of CAP_theorem: in the presence of a network_partition, one must choose between PA (consistency) and EC (availability); otherwise EL (latency) vs C.

nodes.label: partial failure
nodes.def: A condition during transaction execution where an operation fails after prior operations in the same transaction have already modified state; triggers rollback to enforce atomicity

nodes.label: partially committed
nodes.def: A transient transaction_state after the final statement executes but before log records are flushed; failure here triggers rollback.

nodes.label: phantom read anomaly
nodes.def: A specific manifestation of phantom_read in lock-based isolation: gap_lock or predicate_locking violations allow new rows to appear between reads.

nodes.label: postgresql mvcc
nodes.def: PostgreSQL's implementation of snapshot_isolation via transaction_id, version_chain, and VACUUM for garbage_collection_mvcc.

nodes.label: predicate locking
nodes.def: A theoretical locking mechanism that locks the set of rows satisfying a predicate, rather than specific rows or gaps; prevents phantom_read in serializable.

nodes.label: raft consensus
nodes.def: A consensus_protocol designed to be understandable, providing leader election and log replication as an alternative to paxos_consensus.

nodes.label: read after write
nodes.def: A consistency guarantee where a client's own writes are immediately visible to subsequent reads from that same client; a common eventual_consistency_level escape hatch.

nodes.label: read committed allows non repeatable read
nodes.def: read_committed allows non_repeatable_read: the statement_snapshot refreshes at each statement start, so rows read early in a transaction can change.

nodes.label: read committed allows phantom read
nodes.def: read_committed allows phantom_read: newly inserted committed rows can appear in subsequent statement executions within the same transaction.

nodes.label: read committed is stronger than read uncommitted
nodes.def: read_committed provides stronger guarantees than read_uncommitted: it prevents dirty_read that read_uncommitted allows.

nodes.label: read committed is weaker than repeatable read
nodes.def: read_committed provides weaker guarantees than repeatable_read: it permits non_repeatable_read and phantom_read that repeatable_read prevents.

nodes.label: read committed prevents dirty read
nodes.def: read_committed prevents dirty_read: uncommitted changes from other transactions are invisible to statements.

nodes.label: read only snapshot
nodes.def: An isolation_level variant where read transactions use an mvcc snapshot but cannot write, reducing lock contention and enabling certain optimizations.

nodes.label: read phase
nodes.def: The initial phase in optimistic_cc where a transaction reads all needed data and stores read_set for later validation.

nodes.label: read skew
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction reads multiple rows and sees an inconsistent state because another transaction is mid-update on those rows.

nodes.label: read view
nodes.def: The metadata defining which row versions are visible to a transaction in mvcc: transaction_id boundaries and active transaction list.

nodes.label: read write conflict
nodes.def: A conflict where one transaction reads stale data invalidated by another transaction's uncommitted or subsequent write.

nodes.label: recoverable schedule
nodes.def: A schedule where committed transactions never read data written by aborted transactions; a minimal correctness requirement for transaction histories.

nodes.label: redo log
nodes.def: Log records describing changes to be reapplied during recovery to bring the database forward to a consistent state after a crash.

nodes.label: retry logic
nodes.def: Application code that re-executes a transaction_retry on transient failures (deadlock, serialization_failure, lock_timeout) before propagating errors.

nodes.label: saga pattern
nodes.def: A pattern for managing distributed_transaction without ACID atomicity: each step has a compensating_transaction to undo its effects on failure.

nodes.label: savepoint
nodes.def: A named marker within a transaction allowing partial rollback to that point without aborting the entire transaction.

nodes.label: schema lock
nodes.def: A lock held during DDL operations (ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX) that prevents concurrent DML or other schema changes.

nodes.label: select for update
nodes.def: A SQL clause acquiring exclusive_lock on selected rows before returning results, preventing concurrent modifications until commit or rollback.

nodes.label: sequential consistency
nodes.def: A consistency model where all operations appear in a globally consistent order, but that order need not correspond to real time.

nodes.label: serializable schedule
nodes.def: A history of concurrent transaction operations producing the same result as some serial ordering of those transactions.

nodes.label: serializable snapshot isolation
nodes.def: PostgreSQL's serializable_isolation implemented as an SSI extension to snapshot_isolation, detecting and aborting serialization_failure via SSI_detect.

nodes.label: serialization failure
nodes.def: A transaction abort triggered when serializable detects a write_skew or other serializability violation during commit via SSI_detect.

nodes.label: shared lock release
nodes.def: In lock_based_read_committed, shared locks held on rows are released before transaction commit, enabling writers to acquire exclusive locks on those rows.

nodes.label: snapshot
nodes.def: A point-in-time consistent view of the database state presented to a transaction; defined by read_view in mvcc systems or by isolation_level in lock-based systems.

nodes.label: split brain
nodes.def: A failure condition in distributed_locking where a partition causes two nodes to believe they each hold the same lock, leading to data corruption.

nodes.label: sql server snapshot isolation
nodes.def: Microsoft SQL Server's snapshot_isolation using row versioning, distinct from serializable_snapshot_isolation (SI) in PostgreSQL.

nodes.label: ssi detect
nodes.def: The Serialized Snapshot Isolation algorithm that detects dangerous structural dependencies between concurrent transactions to identify write_skew violations.

nodes.label: statement refreshes snapshot
nodes.def: A defining property of read_committed: unlike repeatable_read where the snapshot spans the entire transaction, each statement obtains a fresh snapshot at statement_start.

nodes.label: statement snapshot
nodes.def: The committed state of the database as observed at the moment a statement begins within a read_committed transaction; defines the visible set of rows.

nodes.label: statement start
nodes.def: The point in time when a SQL statement begins execution in a read_committed transaction, establishing which committed changes are visible.

nodes.label: strong consistency
nodes.def: A consistency model where all reads see the most recent committed write; requires coordination and prevents all anomalies at the cost of latency.

nodes.label: t xid
nodes.def: A compact transaction identifier used in row version headers to record which transaction created or deleted a tuple.

nodes.label: thomas write rule
nodes.def: An optimization of basic_timestamp_protocol that allows certain writes to be skipped rather than aborted, improving throughput.

nodes.label: three phase commit
nodes.def: An extension of two_phase_commit that adds a pre-commit phase to avoid blocking when the coordinator fails during the commit phase.

nodes.label: transaction manager
nodes.def: The component coordinating transaction boundaries, lock acquisition, commit, and rollback across database operations.

nodes.label: transaction retry
nodes.def: The process of re-executing a transaction that aborted due to conflict_detection or serialization_failure; may use exponential_backoff.

nodes.label: transaction table
nodes.def: A database internal table tracking the status of all in-flight transactions for visibility_check and recovery purposes.

nodes.label: transaction throughput
nodes.def: The number of transactions per unit time a database can process; directly impacted by lock_contention, lock_granularity, and isolation_level.

nodes.label: two phase commit
nodes.def: A distributed_transaction commit protocol with a prepare phase followed by a commit phase, ensuring atomicity across all participants.

nodes.label: unique lock
nodes.def: A lock acquired automatically when inserting a unique key value; prevents duplicate key violations from concurrent inserts.

nodes.label: vacuum postgresql
nodes.def: PostgreSQL's garbage_collection_mvcc implementation: reclaiming dead tuple versions, freezing old transaction_ids, updating FSM.

nodes.label: validation phase
nodes.def: The phase in optimistic_cc where the committing transaction verifies it has no conflicts with concurrent transactions before making changes visible.

nodes.label: version boundary
nodes.def: In mvcc_read_committed, the version of a row visible to a statement is determined by the most recent committed version as of statement_start.

nodes.label: version chain
nodes.def: A linked list of row versions ordered by transaction_id, enabling a transaction to retrieve the appropriate version from read_view.

nodes.label: version vector
nodes.def: A per-object structure in optimistic_cc tracking which transactions have modified an object, used for conflict detection.

nodes.label: view serializable
nodes.def: A schedule property requiring equivalence to a serial schedule on the same read and write operations; a superset of conflict_serializable, NP-hard to verify.

nodes.label: visibility check
nodes.def: The algorithm determining whether a specific row version is visible to a transaction given its transaction_id and the set of active transactions.

nodes.label: wait die
nodes.def: A deadlock_prevention scheme for wounds_die: an older transaction waits for locks; a younger transaction aborts if it would need to wait (non-preemptive).

nodes.label: wound wait
nodes.def: A deadlock_prevention scheme: an older transaction wounds (aborts) a younger transaction holding a needed lock; the younger waits if older.

nodes.label: write phase
nodes.def: The phase in optimistic_cc where a transaction constructs private write_set before validation against other transactions' read_sets and write_sets.

nodes.label: write skew
nodes.def: An anomaly in snapshot_isolation where two concurrent transactions each read overlapping data, modify disjoint subsets, and both commit successfully despite conflicting.

nodes.label: write snapshots
nodes.def: The set of modifications made by a transaction in mvcc, only visible to other transactions after the transaction commits.
